page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadsv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes 2835 GB of local NVMe storage and supports Premium Storage. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptography accelerations like AES and SHA_NI.

In benchmark testing, the E48ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core processing, evaluated via stress-ng and Geekbench, ranks in the top 10%, aided by the 4.5 GHz clock speed. Memory performance is strong, with read-only cached small-block bandwidth reaching 5034.16 GB/sec and large-block write bandwidth at 103.08 GB/sec. Computational workloads such as gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and image processing also achieve top-tier results. Database operations and Redis SET performance are highly competitive, registering in the top 25% of tested systems. Large-block uncached read bandwidth and prompt processing for larger LLM models (7B and 70B) fall into the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48ads_v7 offers a dense allocation of high-speed memory and local storage relative to its compute capacity, reducing the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive tasks. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and software compilation. The inclusion of fast local storage and AVX-512 vector extensions also makes it viable for vector-heavy calculations and medium-scale machine learning inference.
